NEW YORK, April 20.—Federal officials were today investigating the wreck of the New York Central Railroads crack Lake Shore Limited last evening at Little Falls, N. Y. Reports indicated that the company would be censured for failing to observe I.C.C. rules.

Ickes of the appointment of George Folta, Assistant District Attorney in the First Division, as Alaska attorney for the Department of Interior, a newly created and lucrative position.

Known only to few of the Interior Department's inner circle in the north, Folta was assayed and found favorable for the post even before it was presented to him about two months ago. He started out in Alaska as a clerk in the Steamboat Inspectors office. He studied and became a court reporter—court officials will tell you one of the best ever developed in the north. Kilmartin are drawing up list of registration headquarters in each district. The list will be an- nounced in a day or two.

 The mayor will head a group of local officials which will attend a county meeting in New Haven Mon- day night, at which time repre- sentative of the state selective serv- ice headquarters at Hartford will outline the procedure to be follow ed. tu

 Under present plans, the teach CTS and other volunteers who serve on registration day will work in three shifts. One group will work from a. m. to noon. another from noon to p. m. and the third from p. m. to g p. m.

 The thousands of registration cards will be gathered from the 32 districts and sent to the town clerks office. There they will be filed, ready fo- use by the draft boards. The boards will send out uuestionnaire to men chosen by lot. and from this number the actual draftees from Waterbury will be chosen.
